key_insight: The paper shows that reinforcement learning with patient-specific, partially verifiable rewards can improve an LLM’s sequential treatment-planning reasoning in colon cancer under incomplete clinical information.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support more structured, evidence-aligned treatment recommendation workflows where multiple clinically defensible paths may exist for the same partially observed patient.
method: Formulated oncology treatment planning as an interactive reinforcement learning problem under partial observability.
Built patient-specific, process-aware rewards from real-world clinical decision processes in records.
Optimized Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with GRPO and GDPO to improve information gathering, treatment choice, and reasoning alignment.
evidence_signal: In the reported interactive evaluation, the GDPO-trained policy improved Mean@3 scalar clinical reward by 79.60% over base Llama and exceeded GPT-5.2 by 18.82% while reducing query count during training.
watch_item: Because the reward signal is derived from partially observed real-world records, results may depend on dataset quality, reward design, and how well the simulated environment matches clinical practice.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning In Partially Verifiable Environments for Colon Cancer Treatment Planning
